claim: Kaamatan (Harvest Festival) is Sabah's biggest cultural festival, a Kadazandusun thanksgiving climaxing 30-31 May with state celebrations at KDCA Penampang.
quote: Pesta Kaamatan is an annual harvest festival celebrated by the Kadazandusun ethnicities in Sabah as a thanksgiving celebration for a bountiful harvest. Among the event's highlights are the Sugandoi Competition and the crowning of Unduk Ngadau.

claim: Kaamatan 2026 climaxes 30-31 May, a Sabah-only public holiday, with the state finale at KDCA Penampang 15 minutes from KK city.
quote: Kaamatan is celebrated on May 30-31, 2026 across Sabah. The main state-level celebration takes place at KDCA Penampang, just 15 minutes from Kota Kinabalu city center.

claim: Kaamatan honours the rice spirit and legendary Princess Huminodun; district-level celebrations run through May before the state finale.
quote: Kaamatan is Sabah's harvest festival celebrated on May 30-31, honoring the rice harvest and the legendary Princess Huminodun. The main events take place at KDCA Penampang in Kota Kinabalu.

claim: Harvest Festival (Kaamatan) is gazetted 30-31 May and is a public holiday in Sabah and Labuan only.
quote: Harvest Festival 2026, 2027 and 2028. Kaamatan is a public holiday in Sabah only.

claim: The Kaamatan state festival is held at the KDCA (Kadazandusun Cultural Association) grounds in Penampang, with layout, hours and getting-there guidance.
quote: KDCA Kaamatan Guide: Layout, Hours & How to Get There.

claim: Kaamatan features the Sumazau dance, Magunatip Murut bamboo-pole dance, Sugandoi singing contest and Unduk Ngadau beauty pageant.
quote: Magunatip is the traditional Murut bamboo pole dance where dancers jump, hop, and skip between pairs of bamboo poles that are rhythmically struck together... Daily Sumazau, Magunatip, fire-making demonstrations, butod preparation, and slingshot competitions are held during the festival.

claim: Chinese New Year 2026 falls on 17 February 2026 (Year of the Horse), widely celebrated by KK's large Chinese community.
quote: Chinese New Year 2026 in Malaysia: Traditions, Food & Meaning.

claim: Chinese New Year bazaars run across Malaysia in the weeks before CNY 2026, with festive markets and decorations.
quote: 9 Chinese New Year Markets To Check Out This 2026.

claim: Pesta Kalimaran is the Murut people's state festival held at the Murut Cultural Centre in Tenom (day-trip/overnight from KK), showcasing handicrafts, food and lansaran trampoline.
quote: Pesta Kalimaran is an annual state-level celebration for Murut in Sabah, celebrated during April and held at the Murut Cultural Village in Tenom.

claim: Pesta Kalimaran has been fixed to 31 March each year, with the festival running roughly 26-31 March at the Tenom Murut Cultural Centre.
quote: Pesta Kalimaran has been fixed to March 31 on the Sabah calendar, with the 16th celebration of the festival beginning on March 26 until March 31 at the Tenom Murut Cultural Centre.

claim: Regatta Lepa in Semporna celebrates Bajau Laut sea-gypsy maritime heritage with a parade of decorated lepa boats; traditionally held late April.
quote: The Regatta Lepa festival is a famous boat race taking place every year in April in Semporna... introduced to honour the legacy of the Bajau Laut, a nomadic community of Sea Gypsies.

claim: Regatta Lepa features a water parade of colourful lepa boats, a Lepa beauty pageant, fireworks and the Bajau igal-igal dance; dates vary year to year so verify with Sabah Tourism.
quote: The Regatta Lepa is a water parade of colourfully decorated boats... The festival continues late into the night with the Lepa beauty pageant, fireworks, cultural and traditional shows and games, and the famous igal-igal dance of the Bajau people.

claim: Pesta Rumbia (Sago Festival) in Kuala Penyu, held early July, celebrates the many uses of the sago palm.
quote: The Pesta Rumbia is held at the beginning of July in Kuala Penyu... a celebration of the many uses of the sago, from the bark to the pulp processed and eaten in place of rice.

claim: The Sabah International Folklore Festival (SIFF) runs 24-30 July 2026 at Wisma Budaya in KK, with a KK City Folklore Parade, food/handicraft exhibition and international folk-dance competition.
quote: The Sabah International Folklore Festival is scheduled for July 24 to 30 in 2026... organized at Wisma Budaya Building, Tunku Abdul Rahman Road in Kota Kinabalu.

claim: SIFF is divided into the KK City Folklore Parade, Sabah Traditional Food and Handicraft Exhibition, and International Folk Dance Competition.
quote: The SIFF is divided into three main programmes, namely KK City Folklore Parade, Sabah Traditional Food and Handicraft Exhibition and International Folk Dance Competition.

claim: Tamu Besar Kota Belud, Sabah's largest open-air market, is held the last week of October and features Bajau horsemen ('Cowboys of the East') in traditional dress.
quote: The largest Tamu event occurs during the last week of October each year. One sight to behold is the 'Cowboys of the East', when Bajau horsemen dress their horses and ponies in resplendent traditional attire.

claim: Kota Belud's Bajau Sama horsemen and the symbolic tudung duang craft are an increasingly rare tradition spotlighted at the tamu besar.
quote: The state's oldest tamu besar... also marks a gathering of Bajau horsemen, an increasingly rare sight nowadays. The colorful tudung duang is a symbolic traditional craft unique to the Bajau Sama of Kota Belud.

claim: Tamu Kota Belud is the oldest tamu in Sabah, started in 1878, with the annual Tamu Besar normally a weekend event.
quote: Tamu Kota Belud is the oldest tamu in Sabah, started by William Pretyman, the first British resident in Tempasuk village on December 13, 1878. The annual event is usually celebrated for two days, during a weekend.

claim: Sabah State Museum is open daily 9am-5pm; entry is RM2 for Malaysians and RM15 for non-Malaysians, with free entry for students in uniform, seniors, disabled visitors and taxi drivers.
quote: Malaysian guests pay RM2.00, while non-Malaysian guests pay RM15.00. Special categories including students in uniform, disabled guests, senior guests, and taxi drivers can enter for free. Open daily from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm.

claim: The Sabah Museum complex includes the Rungus-longhouse-shaped main building, Science & Technology Centre, Heritage Village, Ethno-Botanical Garden and Sabah Islamic Civilization Museum.
quote: The Sabah Museum Complex comprises the Main Building, the Science and Technology Centre, the Heritage Village, Ethno-Botanical Garden and the Sabah Islamic Civilization Museum, all located just off Jalan Penampang.

claim: The Heritage Village displays traditional Sabah houses including a Bajau house with wedding dais, a Murut longhouse with lansaran trampoline, a Chinese farmhouse and a House of Skulls.
quote: Among them are a Bajau House complete with a wedding dais, a Murut longhouse with a lansaran (trampoline), a Chinese farmhouse with earthen floor, a Bamboo House and a House of Skulls.

claim: The main museum building, modelled on a Rungus longhouse, holds Ethnography, Natural History, Ceramics, Archaeology and History galleries.
quote: The Main Building is designed after a traditional Rungus longhouse; inside are the Ethnography, Natural History, Ceramics, Archaeology and History Galleries.

claim: Sabah Art Gallery, in a distinctive basket-shaped building, mounts 12+ exhibitions yearly with over 3,000 paintings, carvings and sculptures.
quote: The gallery is housed in a distinctive basket-shaped building and showcases more than 12 exhibitions annually with over 3,000 paintings, carvings, and sculptures featured.

claim: Sabah Art Gallery opens Tuesday-Sunday 9am-4pm (closed Monday); adults RM15, children 7-12 RM10, under-7 free.
quote: Open from 9:00 AM - 4:00 PM Tuesday to Sunday, closed on Mondays. Children (7-12) RM 10, adults (13+) RM 15, free entrance for children under 7.

claim: Sabah Art Gallery (Balai Seni Lukis Sabah) is the state's main contemporary-art venue showcasing local Sabahan artists.
quote: Sabah Art Gallery, a Basket of Creativity and Imagination.

claim: Mari Mari Cultural Village (rainforest just outside KK) tickets are RM130 adult / RM110 child for international visitors (RM110/RM100 Malaysian), tours at 10am and 2pm, covering five tribes with a Sabahan buffet.
quote: Malaysian RM110 adult / RM100 child; International RM130 adult / RM110 child; free for children 4 and under. Tours at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM. Tribes: Kadazan-Dusun, Rungus, Lundayeh, Bajau, Murut. Includes an authentic Sabahan buffet meal.

claim: Mari Mari is a living museum where visitors meet five indigenous tribes of North Borneo with demonstrations of fire-starting, blowpipe hunting and traditional cooking.
quote: Mari Mari Cultural Village is a living museum near Kota Kinabalu where you can meet 5 indigenous tribes of North Borneo. Daily guided tours are offered at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM.

claim: Monsopiad Heritage Village in Penampang (16km from KK) is Sabah's only living museum to a Kadazandusun headhunter, with the House of Skulls displaying 42 trophy skulls; open 9am-5pm with dances at 9, 11, 2 and 4.
quote: Monsopiad Heritage Village is the only living museum in Sabah commemorating the life of fearsome head-hunter warrior 'Monsopiad'. The House of Skulls has all 42 'trophies' on display. Timing 09:00-17:00, dances at 9am, 11am, 2pm & 4pm.

claim: Monsopiad packages must be pre-booked (walk-ins not accepted), and include a guided tour, House of Skulls visit and cultural show.
quote: Pre-booked at least two (2) weeks in advance required for all packages. Visit to legendary House of Skulls included in most packages.

claim: Monsopiad admission for adult foreign tourists is about RM65 (includes guided tour and cultural activities); advance booking required.
quote: For foreign tourists, the adult ticket price is RM65... entrance fee includes Guided Tour & Activities.

claim: Linangkit Cultural Village in Tuaran is a Dusun Lotud living museum named after the Lotud linangkit embroidery, where guests try weaving, cooking, dancing and ceremonies.
quote: The village is named after the traditional Lotud embroidery called linangkit. Located in Tuaran, this living museum preserves traditions... Guests can try weaving, cooking, dancing, and even joining traditional ceremonies.

claim: Linangkit is a Sabah hand needle-weaving technique forming dense colourful knotted motifs used on several Indigenous groups' costumes.
quote: The linangkit technique uses a needle and threads to create a system of tiny intricately connected identical knots to form a dense fabric of colourful motifs, used on the costumes of several Indigenous groups in Sabah.

claim: Kampung Bavanggazo near Kudat (~2hr from KK) is the main Rungus longhouse where visitors see beadwork and can stay overnight.
quote: Kampung Bavanggazo (Rungus Longhouse) near Kudat... a living museum preserving the traditional Rungus way of life.

claim: Rungus longhouse stays in Kudat offer beadmaking, pandan-mat weaving, basket-making, gong-music storytelling and home-cooked meals.
quote: Guests can weave mats from pandan leaves, try beadwork, or learn the delicate art of basket-making, with evening storytelling sessions often accompanied by the deep rhythms of gong music.

claim: The Rungus, a Kadazan-Dusun sub-group of the Kudat peninsula, are renowned for distinctive bead necklaces and brass coil work.
quote: The Rungus people live primarily in the Kudat district... renowned throughout Southeast Asia for their distinctive bead jewelry and brass coil work.

claim: Gaya Street Sunday Market (city centre) runs Sundays roughly 6am-1pm selling crafts, batik, fruit, snacks, antiques, orchids, pearls and pets.
quote: The street fair starts as early as 6.00am and ends at 1.00pm... arts and crafts, batik sarongs, footwear, fruits and flowers, local snacks, antiques and souvenirs, to even pets and herbs.

claim: Gaya Street Sunday market also offers reflexology by blind masseurs from the Sabah Society for the Blind and on-the-spot portrait artists.
quote: Visitors can also get reflexology and foot massage treatments by trained blind masseurs from the Sabah Society for the Blind, and local artists put up their easel ready to take commission art.

claim: The Filipino/Handicraft Market (Anjung Kinabalu) on KK's waterfront sells pearls, woven bags, wood carvings and traditional accessories; bargaining expected, and much is mass-produced.
quote: Famous for handicrafts such as pearls, woven bags, wood carvings, and traditional accessories... can be underwhelming if you're seeking authentic, locally made crafts, as many items are mass-produced imports.

claim: KK's waterfront Anjung Kinabalu groups a wet market, night market, handicraft complex and hawker centre; seafood stalls peak 5-10pm.
quote: Anjung Kinabalu, or Filipino Night Market, is along the city's waterfront which includes a wet market, night market, handicraft complex & a hawker centre. Evening (5 PM-10 PM): seafood stalls come alive.

claim: Tamu are rotating weekly open-air markets across Sabah districts: Donggongon (Penampang) on Thursday and Friday, Tuaran on Sunday.
quote: Donggongon Tamu takes place every Thursday and Friday (6am-6pm). Tuaran tamu is held on Sunday.

claim: The tamu is Sabah's traditional rotating market and cultural meeting place selling produce, handicrafts, local food and livestock.
quote: Tamu, the traditional market of Sabah... a gathering for the local community to trade, showcase culture, and celebrate Sabah's heritage.

claim: Songket Restaurant in KK stages a live Sabah/Malaysian cultural dance show Monday-Saturday 8.30-9.15pm.
quote: Dance performances are available 6x per week from 8.30pm-9.15pm on Mondays to Saturdays, with dance also available for other time slots or Sundays for a small additional fee.

claim: The Sabah Cultural Board offers official cultural show packages featuring state traditional dances and music.
quote: Cultural Show Package | Sabah Cultural Board.

claim: Evening dinner-and-cultural-show tours (e.g. Kampung Nelayan floating seafood restaurant) feature Sumazau, Magunatip, Joget and Zapin dances with audience participation.
quote: Kampung Nelayan Floating Seafood Market Restaurant offers dinner with Sabah Cultural Shows including Sumazau, Mengilok, Magunatip, Joget, Zapin and other Malaysian dances.

claim: Signal Hill is the renovated hilltop precinct bundling the Atkinson Clock Tower, Signal Hill Trail treetop walkway and Observatory Tower into one ticketed attraction.
quote: Signal Hill - Official Ticket Information | Atkinson Clock Tower & Trail.

claim: The Atkinson Clock Tower, KK's oldest standing structure (commissioned 1905, built without nails), reopened after a multimillion-ringgit facelift as the anchor of the Signal Hill precinct.
quote: Following a multimillion-ringgit facelift completed late last year, Kota Kinabalu's oldest landmark has re-emerged as the anchor of a refreshed attraction... complete with a 500m treetop walkway linking the tower to the Observatory.

claim: The integrated Atkinson Clock Tower Square + Signal Hill Trail attraction was officially launched by DBKK on 10 November 2025, with a 500m treetop walkway.
quote: This integrated heritage-and-nature attraction was officially launched by Dewan Bandaraya Kota Kinabalu (DBKK) on 10 November 2025.

claim: The KK Heritage Walk covers Gaya Street, Beach Street and Jesselton Point, starting at the Sabah Tourism Board building, recounting Jesselton's WWII destruction and post-war rebuild.
quote: The Kota Kinabalu Heritage Walk is centred around three areas, namely Gaya Street, Beach Street and Jesselton Point... the Atkinson Clock Tower remains the oldest building in Kota Kinabalu.

claim: The licensed-guide heritage walk leaves the Sabah Tourism Board building on Gaya Street on Wednesdays (English) and Saturdays (Mandarin) and runs about 2 hours.
quote: Heritage walking tours commence at the Sabah Tourism Board building in Gaya Street on Wednesdays (in English) and Saturdays (in Mandarin). The tours run approximately 2 hours.

claim: Kota Kinabalu City Mosque ('floating mosque') sits on a man-made lagoon; non-Muslim visitors pay ~RM5, must dress modestly (robes/headscarves provided) and avoid Fridays.
quote: The Kota Kinabalu City Mosque is often referred to as the floating mosque... visitors must dress modestly; long robes and headscarves are provided. Do not come on Fridays. It is about 5 ringgit to visit.

claim: Pu Tuo Si (Puh Toh Tze) off Tuaran Road, built 1980 with a Guanyin statue, is KK's main Chinese temple and a focal point during Chinese New Year.
quote: Pu Tuo Si Temple (also called Puh Toh Tze Temple) is a Buddhist temple located off Tuaran Road in Kota Kinabalu... built in 1980 with a statue of Guanyin at the entrance. It is the main Chinese temple for the city.

claim: Mengkabong Water Village near Tuaran is a Bajau ('sea gypsy') stilt-house settlement over the water, visited on river-cruise day trips from KK.
quote: Mengkabong Water Village is home to the Bajaus, an indigenous group also known as Sabah's sea gypsies. They live in wooden houses built on stilts that hover above water.

claim: In June 2026, 1 Malaysian ringgit was worth roughly EUR 0.21 (RM1 ≈ €0.21), so RM10 ≈ €2.10.
quote: As of June 8, 2026, the rate was RM1 = EUR0.2133; as of June 2, 2026, 1 Malaysian Ringgit equals 0.2169 Euros.
